fn Power(base: Int, exponent: Int) -> Int
  requires (exponent >= 0)
  ensures (result == (if (exponent == 0) then 1 else (base * Power(base, (exponent - 1)))))
  effects pure
  example (Power(0, 0) == 1)
  example (Power(0, 1) == 0)
{
  if (exponent == 0) then 1 else (base * Power(base, (exponent - 1)))
}

fn PowerOfListElements(l: List[Int], n: Int) -> List[Int]
  requires (n >= 0)
  ensures (len(result) == len(l))
  ensures forall i in 0..len(l): (result[i] == Power(l[i], n))
  effects pure
  example (PowerOfListElements([], 0) == [])
{
  []
}
